topic: Neural Networks: The Blueprint of Artificial Intelligence

sections.title: The Big Picture: Bio-inspiration to Computation
lecture_lines: Neural networks are models inspired by the human brain.
Computers process data as patterns of numerical values.
We map these input patterns to specific output predictions.
animations: Fade in a stylized brain [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/brain.svg] (#88CCEE) and morph it into a network of nodes (#FFFFFF). self.wait(2.0)
Fade in a vector of numbers [0.1, 0.9, 0.4] in yellow (#FFEE55) representing raw data. self.wait(1.5)
Create a green (#00FF00) arrow from the vector to a 'Cat' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cat.png] prediction label. self.wait(2.0)

sections.title: The Perceptron: The Single Neuron
lecture_lines: A neuron is the basic unit of neural networks.
Weights adjust the importance of each incoming signal.
The bias sets a threshold for the neuron's activation.
animations: Create a central neuron using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/neuron.svg] with three input lines entering it. self.wait(1.5)
Label input lines with 'w1', 'w2', 'w3' in cyan (#00FFFF) and bold 'w1' to show high importance. self.wait(2.0)
Display a yellow '+ b' (#FFCC00) inside the neuron circle to represent bias. self.wait(1.5)

sections.title: The Mathematical Engine: Summation and Activation
lecture_lines: First, we multiply every input by its weight.
Next, we sum these products and add the bias.
This total enters a gate called an activation function.
Sigmoid or ReLU functions determine the neuron's final output.
This math decides if a signal is strong enough.
animations: Display the equation 'z = Σ(x * w) + b' in white (#FFFFFF) at the center. self.wait(2.0)
Morph the 'Σ' symbol into a magenta (#FF00FF) Sigmoid activation curve. self.wait(2.0)
Highlight the upper region of the Sigmoid curve in green (#00FF00) to indicate activation. self.wait(1.5)

sections.title: The Architecture: Layers and Depth
lecture_lines: Neurons organize into input, hidden, and output layers.
Multiple hidden layers create what we call deep learning.
Each layer extracts increasingly complex features from the data.
animations: Show three columns of nodes: Input (blue #5555FF), Hidden (white #FFFFFF), and Output (green #00FF00). self.wait(2.0)
Duplicate the hidden layer column three times to visualize 'Deep Learning' depth. self.wait(2.0)
Flash cyan (#00FFFF) on the first layer, then yellow (#FFCC00) on the second to show hierarchical processing. self.wait(1.5)

sections.title: Information Flow: Forward Propagation
lecture_lines: Data flows forward through the network's layers.
Each layer's output becomes the input for the next.
Thousands of simple calculations cascade toward a final result.
The output layer represents probabilities for different outcomes.
High values indicate the network's most likely prediction.
animations: An image of the number '7' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/seven.svg] passes through the network, causing nodes to glow sequentially. self.wait(2.0)
Draw white (#FFFFFF) glowing arrows connecting nodes layer-by-layer to show signal flow. self.wait(2.0)
Highlight the specific '7' node in the green (#00FF00) output layer with a pulse effect. self.wait(1.5)

sections.title: The Feedback Loop: How Networks Learn
lecture_lines: Loss measures the difference between prediction and reality.
We use this error to refine the network's performance.
The algorithm slightly adjusts weights to reduce future mistakes.
This iterative process is how a machine actually learns.
With enough practice, the model achieves high accuracy.
animations: Display a red (#FF0000) 'X' mark over an incorrect prediction node. self.wait(1.5)
Show weights 'w' shifting values with cyan (#00FFFF) arrows to indicate adjustment. self.wait(2.0)
Morph the red 'X' mark into a green (#00FF00) check mark as the network learns. self.wait(2.0)
